section.title: Activity
section.para: With a partner, discuss the following situations and equations. For each, consider:

list.item: What does the solution mean in the context of the situation?
Are the given values solutions?

section.para: If operations are applied correctly, the solution to an equation is also the solution to all equations equivalent to it. If operations are incorrectly applied, the solution of each equation is different.
For numbers 1 and 2, use the following situation and equation:
Noah is buying a pair of jeans and using a coupon for 10% off. The total price is $56.70, which includes $2.70 in sales tax. Noah’s purchase can be modeled by the equation:

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
The solution is the price of a pair of jeans.

list.item: What does the solution to the equation mean in this situation?

div.para: Compare your answer:
Your answer may vary, but here are some samples.

70 can be substituted into the equation to make a false statement:
\(70−0.1(70)+2.70=56.70\)
\(65.70 ≠ 56.70\) ❌

60 can be substituted into the equation to make a true statement:
\( 60−0.1(60)+2.70=56.70\)
\(56.70=56.70\) \(\checkmark\)

Here are some equations that are related to \(x−0.1x+2.70=56.70\). Each equation is a result of performing one or more moves on that original equation. Each can also be interpreted in terms of Noah’s purchase.
For numbers 3–5, use the equation \(100x−10x+270=5,670\).

list.item: How can you verify that 70 is not a solution but 60 is the solution?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
Every term was multiplied by 100. The equation is equivalent to Noah’s equation.

list.item: What was done to Noah’s equation to make this one?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
The price is now expressed in cents instead of dollars.

list.item: What is the interpretation of this new equation?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
60 is a solution in both equations.
For numbers 6–8, use the equation \(x−0.1x=54\).

list.item: Is the solution the same?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
Subtract 2.70 from both sides of the equation. The equation is equivalent to Noah’s equation.

list.item: What was done to Noah’s equation to make this one?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
The price is still in dollars.

list.item: What is the interpretation of this new equation?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
60 is a solution in both equations.
For numbers 9–11, use the equation \(0.9x+2.70=56.70\).

list.item: Is the solution the same?

div.para: Compare your answer:

Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
The terms \(x\) and 0.1x were correctly combined to create an equivalent equation to Noah’s original equation.

list.item: What was done to Noah’s equation to make this one?

div.para: Compare your answer:
Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
10% off means paying 90% of the original price. 90% of the original price plus sales tax is $56.70.

list.item: What is the interpretation of this new equation?

div.para: Compare your answer:
Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
60 is a solution in both equations.

list.item: Is the solution the same?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
Sales tax was not included on the left but was included on the right. This equation is not equivalent to Noah’s original equation.

list.item: What was done to Noah’s equation to make this one?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
The price after using the coupon for 10% off before sales tax is not the same as the price after using the coupon for 10% off including the sales tax, $56.70.

list.item: What is the interpretation of this new equation?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
60 is not a solution to this equation.

list.item: Is the solution the same?

div.para:
Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
Subtract 2.70 from the left and add 2.70 to the right.

list.item: What was done to Noah’s equation to make this one?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
The same operation must be done to both sides of an equation to keep it balanced and to create an equivalent equation. The price after using the coupon for 10% off is not equal to 56.70 plus tax.

60 is not a solution to this equation.

list.item: What was done to Noah’s equation to make this one?

div.para:
Your answer may vary, but here is a sample.
Two pairs of jeans after the 10% discount and sales tax cost 56.70.

list.item: What is the interpretation of this new equation?

list.item: Is the solution the same?
Based on your work above, which of the six equations are equivalent to the original equation, \(x−0.1x+2.70=56.70\)? Select the three equations that are equivalent to the original.
